newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa for leaving hospital, doctors say no.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa for leaving hospital, doctors say no.

text.p: Feeling fit and cheerful, Mother Teresa is pressing to leave hospital but doctors said on Tuesday the revered missionary must first regain more strength from her two-week fight against malaria and pneumonia.
"She is pressing us everyday to release her," said S.K. Sen, medical director at Calcutta's Woodlands Nursing Home where the Nobel Peace Prize winner has been admitted for a fortnight.

"It is virtually a tug of war every day, and every day we are telling her that we are going to release her tomorrow," the doctor, part of a team of specialists monitoring the missionary's condition, told reporters.

The 86-year-old nun, called the Saint of the Gutters for her work with the poor and destitute, was taken to hospital on August 20 and suffered heart failure while in intensive care. She has been diagnosed with malaria and mild pneumonia.
Over the past week, Mother Teresa's health has steadily improved, and she has begun urging doctors to let her return to her Missionaries of Charity religious order.
"I am fit enough," Sen quoted Mother Teresa as saying. "Nothing will happen to me. I have a pacemaker." She was fitted with a pacemaker in 1989.
Sen said Mother Teresa was showing steady improvement but her heart beat remained irregular. "She is alert and cheerful," the doctor said.
Asked when she would be released, Sen said: "It depends on how long we take to make her a little bit stronger."
The hospital has provided Mother Teresa with an altar and a small statue of Jesus Christ inside the intensive care unit, Sen said. "She gets tremendous powers from the prayers," he said.
